title: TScan axes 75% of workforce, prioritizes solid tumor program
snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

title: 10 life sciences startups selected for accelerator program
snippet: Seven of the 10 companies participating in the fall cohorts of MassBio and SCbio’s Drive program are based in the United States, including four in Massachusetts.

title: Biotech is back, with H1 progress smoothing glide path through end of year: Truist
snippet: With M&A rising, venture capital returning and policy risks easing, biotech is on a positive trajectory following a prolonged post-pandemic slump, Truist Securities declared after a survey of sector leaders.

title: Pfizer punts Seagen ADC, further muddying value of the $43B buyout
snippet: The co-development deal comes after Pfizer reported a late-stage failure for a Seagen asset and the discontinuation of another investigational therapy developed by the company as a subsidiary of the pharma.

title: AbbVie’s T cell engager delivers survival benefit in Phase 3 multiple myeloma study
snippet: AbbVie’s etentamig has a relatively cleaner safety profile and an administration schedule that could give it an edge over other BCMA-targeting multiple myeloma therapies on the market, according to BMO Capital Markets.

title: FDA approves Ionis’ antisense drug as first targeted therapy for Alexander disease
snippet: Zanvastro, an antisense oligonucleotide therapy, represents the first independent neurology launch for Ionis Pharmaceuticals, which intends to leverage the foothold for more approvals in rare neurodegenerative diseases, including Angelman syndrome.

title: TScan cuts 75% of workforce while shifting focus to solid tumor program
snippet: TScan Therapeutics is looking for strategic partnerships for its heme and autoimmune programs while working to advance two in vivo T cell therapy candidates into investigational new drug–enabling studies.

title: RevMed’s newly approved Rasonque could ‘hold up’ in non-small cell lung cancer
snippet: The data, which come from a subgroup in an earlier trial that Truist Securities called “the most relevant” to Revolution Medicines’ ongoing Phase 3 test in RAS mutant NSCLC, showed a 42% overall response rate and overall survival of 16 months.

title: US to grant up to $125M for personalized RNA manufacturing innovation
snippet: A new program from ARPA-H has devoted funding to make individualized RNA-based genetic medicine more efficient to produce and improve accessibility.

title: Summit, Akeso’s ivonescimab bests Merck’s Keytruda in China trial—again
snippet: New Phase 3 data show that Summit Therapeutics and Akeso’s PD-1/VEGF therapy improved overall survival in patients with a type of lung cancer as compared to Merck’s Keytruda but the results will need to be replicated in non-Chinese patients.

title: GSK inks another Asia alliance, betting up to $1.3B for HUTCHMED’s cancer therapy
snippet: For $110 million upfront, GSK will have the exclusive global right to advance HMPL-A830, which combines an EGFR-targeting antibody with a small-molecule KRAS blocker. The asset will be studied for colorectal, pancreatic and lung cancer.

title: Ultragenyx’s 'high-risk' Angelman bet fails, cratering stock and forcing strategic review
snippet: The success of apazunersen in a Phase 3 trial for Angelman syndrome was a key driver of Ultragenyx’s value, according to William Blair, and the asset’s failure robs the biotech of any meaningful near-term milestones.

title: Replimune’s melanoma drug would have been rejected again if not for senior CBER official
snippet: The FDA’s primary review team found that Replimune hadn’t sufficiently addressed deficiencies that had been pointed out in the two prior rejection letters for the melanoma therapy Tudriqev.

title: Breaking borders: Building biotech scale in Benelux
snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from Christina Takke, managing partner at V-Bio Ventures and Mariette van der Velden-Roesink, founding partner at Curie Capital. We explore why the Benelux region remains scientifically strong, but investment fragmented, and what it will take to turn it into a more unified bio...

title: The top 12 companies hiring in biopharma now
snippet: Looking for a biopharma job? Check out the BioSpace list of 12 top companies hiring life sciences professionals like you.

title: Biopharma needs more data scientists. Who's getting hired?
snippet: With U.S. data science jobs projected to grow 35% over the next decade, a recruiter and talent strategy director discuss the qualifications, technical skills and mindset needed to land these coveted positions.

title: Capricor, Replimune illustrate why FDA must listen to rare disease specialists
snippet: Last month’s FDA advisory committee meetings for therapies developed by Capricor Therapeutics and Replimune effectively illustrate the different outcomes for patients when the agency prioritizes specialization in its reviews.

title: FDA raises bar for foreign site inspections as China trials surge
snippet: Inspection access is not “an administrative footnote,” leaders of key FDA divisions wrote in an editorial on Wednesday vowing to expand oversight of foreign clinical trial sites.

title: Follow the money: How funding announcements can help identify jobs before they’re posted
snippet: Funding announcements can signal future hiring activity, giving biotech professionals a chance to build relationships before positions are posted. Industry experts share how to identify the funding events, milestones and company indicators most likely to lead to new jobs.

title: UniQure files for FDA, UK approval of first gene therapy for Huntington’s disease
snippet: The biologics license application follows months of public speculation—and regulatory reversals—for uniQure’s AMT-130. If accepted by the FDA for priority review, approval could come in the second quarter of 2027.

title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.

title: Biotech’s China problem: An issue of national security or economic value for the US?
snippet: Congressional letters sent to the CEOs of Eli Lilly, Pfizer, Merck, BMS and AbbVie this week voicing concerns about the pharmas' clinical trials in China highlight an ongoing discrepancy in how government and industry think about the rise of the Asian country’s biotech industry.

title: BIO 2026: Cell and gene therapy sector must break the mold to thrive
snippet: If cell and gene therapy makers are going to achieve their mission to improve patients’ lives, the industry must come together to share information across stakeholders, from regulators to manufacturers to payers.

title: At FDA, ‘caretaker mode’ is better than power trip mode
snippet: UniQure’s planned third-quarter submission for its Huntington’s disease gene therapy may be a harbinger of a more flexible FDA under acting commissioner Kyle Diamantas—but how long will it last? And how can companies be sure these positive decisions won’t just be reversed?
